messages:
sam: quick sync wondering about SLO slider placement on the Capacity page. current mock puts the slider inline inside each pool card. alternatives: modal on click, or a shared top-level SLO rail per project. opinions? :thinking_face: jordan: inline feels discoverable but it eats vertical space. project-level rail reduces repetition but hides per-pool nuance. my gut: show compact inline preview + a single expanded rail when you click "Edit SLOs". ashley: agree with Jordan. we could show a micro summary in the card: a tiny horizontal bar + value (e.g., "SLO 95%: 150ms") and clicking expands a slide-over to edit. helps density and avoids repeating full sliders. maria: accessibility + keyboard thoughts: if clicking expands a slide-over, set focus to the first interactive control inside and trap focus. slide-over should expose `role=\"dialog\"` + `aria-modal=\"true\"` and `aria-labelledby` referencing the SLO heading. kevin: copy consideration: users often confuse "SLO" vs "target latency". propose these microcopy options for the slide-over header: - Option 1: "Service Level Objective (SLO) — target success & latency" - Option 2: "SLO target — keep response times below" - Option 3: "Target latency & availability" which is clearer for non-ML folks? jordan: Option 3 is simplest but maybe too vague. Option 1 is explicit but long. we can show short header + subline explaining it. e.g., header: "SLO target" subline: "Thresholds that trigger autoscaling and guardrails". sam: good. separate copy ask: guardrail tooltip when slider approaches extremes. currently we show a red chip when SLO <= 5% or >= 99%. need short tooltip text for the warning. suggestions? kevin: drafts: - "Low SLOs may reduce baseline capacity; consider a minimum pool size." - "Very high SLOs can cause cost spikes during traffic bursts." - "Set a guardrail to ensure baseline capacity when SLO is strict." maria: keep it short. my edit: - For low: "Low SLO: may drop baseline capacity. Consider a min." - For high: "High SLO: could increase cost during spikes. Add limits." ashley: UX pattern idea: show an unobtrusive suggestion pill: "Suggest: min=2 based on last 7d 95th pct" with a small `Apply suggestion` action. makes it actionable rather than just scary copy. jordan: where do suggestions come from? we should add a short explanation: "Based on observed peak CPU/mem and 95th p95 latency over last 7 days." need cross-team sign-off for the algorithm text. kevin: noted. Related: keyboard interaction for the slider. propose: left/right arrow + shift for 10, page up/down for 50. announce changes with `aria-live=\"polite\"` message: "SLO target set to 92%". Also when suggestion pill appears, include `aria-atomic=true` so screen readers notice it. maria: technical accessibility nit: the visual slider must expose value via `role=slider` and `aria-valuetext` with units. example snippet: ```
``` ux-bot: heuristic: preferred pattern is "preview inline + slide-over edit" for density target <= 48px per row. current inline full sliders average 64px. slide-over flow reduces row height by ~20px. sam: action list: 1) Ashley to mock compact inline preview + slide-over edit 2) Kevin to finalize guardrail tooltip copy and suggestion pill text 3) Maria to add aria snippets to spec and share snippet file 4) Jordan to draft algorithm blurb for suggestion source and ping data team 5) UX-bot to re-run density heuristic after mocks. deadline: Fri EOD. ashley: on it. I'll post two variants: "preview with microbar" and "preview with value-only" frames by Thursday AM. kevin: I'll post final microcopy + two small examples for toast/tooltip. maria: I'll validate keyboard behavior before sign-off. ux-bot: reminder set: density re-check scheduled 2026-03-27T16:00Z and results will be posted here.
